extracted.intended_audience: Peer reviewers / referees for Nature Reviews journals (e.g., Nature Reviews Molecular Cell Biology)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing a referee report for manuscripts submitted to Nature Reviews journals, covering publication criteria, required elements of a report, how to provide constructive feedback, confidential comments to editors, and submission instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of scope and aim of the article
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity of scope and aim of the article
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess whether the manuscript clearly states its scope and aims; this is a core factor editors consider when deciding if the manuscript meets the journal’s criteria for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical presentation and discussion of ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Logical presentation and discussion of ideas
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the manuscript presents ideas in a coherent, logically ordered manner and whether the discussion follows from presented evidence and arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: New insight into recent advances
rubrics_metrics.description: New insight into recent advances
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the manuscript provides new or synthetic insight into recent research and advances in the field, beyond merely summarizing existing literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility to a wide audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Accessibility of the article to a wide audience, including readers who are not specialists in the field
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the article is written and structured so that non-specialist readers can understand the main messages; readability and appropriate context are important for Nature Reviews readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair and accurate discussion of the literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Fair and accurate discussion of the literature
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for balanced, unbiased coverage of relevant literature and accurate representation of others' findings; flag omissions or misrepresentations and suggest important studies to include if missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and accuracy of display items
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity and accuracy of display items
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an opinion on whether boxes, figures and tables are suitable and useful for the manuscript’s arguments. Focus on the scientific content and accuracy of display items rather than their visual polish (figures will be redrawn later).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate, well‑curated, up‑to‑date references
rubrics_metrics.description: References that are appropriate, well‑curated, up‑to‑date and fit the scope of the article
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether references are relevant, current, balanced and comprehensive for the article’s scope; where relevant, provide citations that affect the manuscript’s significance or accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit to article type and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitability of content, tone and structure for the specific article type (e.g., Review, Evidence‑Based Guideline, Consensus Statement, Primer, Perspective)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take into account the specific article type: e.g., a Review should provide a balanced overview and authoritative discussion, whereas a Perspective may express opinion but must remain fair and not ignore alternative views. Reviewers will receive more specific instructions from editors about format expectations and should follow those.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on scientific soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary purpose is to provide feedback on the soundness of the manuscript
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the correctness and rigor of arguments and interpretations. Reviewers are not required to make a publication recommendation, though they may present arguments for and against publication; the emphasis is on identifying flaws and strengths that affect scientific soundness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key points — concise overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Your overview of the key messages of the article, in your own words, highlighting what you find significant or notable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize the main messages in a short paragraph to orient editors and authors; this helps clarify what you perceive as the manuscript’s contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insight — evaluation of interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the interpretation of recent advances and the level of insight given by the authors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the authors’ interpretations are appropriate and insightful. If there are flaws that prohibit publication, describe them in detail so authors and editors can understand the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance — assessment of impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Your view on the potential significance of the article and its conclusions for the field
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State how the manuscript’s conclusions may affect the field. If other published findings undermine the manuscript’s significance, provide relevant references to support that view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and context in the text
rubrics_metrics.description: Your view on the clarity and accessibility of the text, and whether the discussion has been provided with sufficient context and consideration of previous work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on whether the narrative provides adequate background and context. Note that reviewers are not asked to comment on minor language issues (spelling or grammar). Focus on conceptual clarity and contextualization.

rubrics_metrics.name: References — balance and coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Your view on whether the manuscript references the literature appropriately
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of balance and ensure important studies within the scope are fairly represented. Suggest additions or removals if the citation set is biased or incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display items — scientific suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Your opinion on the suitability and usefulness of display items in the manuscript, including boxes, figures and tables
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether display items help convey the science effectively. Do not focus on figure aesthetics or final artwork quality, since figures will be redrawn at a later stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested improvements — scope‑limited
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestions for additional discussion that could help strengthen the work and make it suitable for publication in the journal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer concrete, specific suggestions that are limited to changes that can reasonably be addressed in a revision. Exclude suggestions that would significantly change the scope of the manuscript; the editor will judge which suggestions to pass to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare limits of expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Please indicate any particular part of the manuscript that you feel is outside the scope of your expertise, or that you were unable to assess fully
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State sections or topics you could not assess so editors can weigh your comments appropriately and seek additional expertise if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive intent and specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach peer review with a sincere intention to help the authors improve; suggest specific improvements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nearly all submissions have weaknesses; the most helpful reports give actionable, specific guidance that authors can use to improve the work, whether or not it will ultimately be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: direct but respectful
rubrics_metrics.description: You should be direct in your report, but you should also maintain a respectful tone
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be frank about flaws, but avoid rude or abusive language. Review text is transmitted to authors uncensored; editors may edit reports only to remove offensive language or comments that reveal confidential information about other matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use confidential comments to editors appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential comments to the editor may be the appropriate place to discuss sensitive information or opinions, including any potential ethical issues with the work, or information that cannot be shared with other reviewers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include issues such as potential ethical concerns, prior interactions with the manuscript at another journal, or other sensitive matters in the confidential box. Do not use confidential comments to contradict what you tell authors; confidential comments should not in any way contradict the comments to the authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid revealing confidential or irrelevant information
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential information about other matters should not be revealed in author-facing comments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may remove content revealing confidential information or offensive language; use the confidential-to-editor field for sensitive material rather than including it in comments to authors.
